In this episode: What to check before you start
What to write on the noteboard
How to read the countdown clock
How to use the last ten minutes
Before you start: Photo ID: government-issued, unexpired, exact registration name
Online: stay in webcam view, clear desk, nobody else
No phones, smart watches, headphones or recorders
Be ready early: late past the window forfeits the fee
Accept the confidentiality agreement; a proper breakfast
The noteboard: Time left: Q20 @ 1:23 · Q40 @ 0:47 · Q60 @ 0:10; ahead → bank it, behind → flag faster
Confident citation → check the source · simple volume → faster, cheaper model
"Don't keep it" → fix the data first · skip → proportionate step
Long chat drifting → summarise, restart, or persist in a Project · technical build → escalate
Fluent is not correct · sized to the stakes
Item formats: Multiple response: read how many to pick first
Dropdown statements: each one is its own item
No domain labels: read the stakes in every stem
When an item rattles you: Best answer, flag it, move on
Policy, personal data or a named audience: slow down
Three hard in a row: one breath, then read the last line first
Behind at a checkpoint: past 2 minutes, answer and flag
The last ten minutes: Change an answer only for a reason in the stem
